sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul. 2008 (pre-publication draft). Vowel harmony in Kimaragang. Draft p. 4.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not about Klias River Kadazan. Family-level generalization only: 'A number of Sabah languages outside of the Dusunic family have similar processes which neutralize non-high vowels in pre-stress syllables, and most if not all of these languages have regular penultimate stress. Labuk Kadazan (Hurlbut, 1981).. also has regular penultimate stress.. As in Penampang Kadazan (Miller, 1993), stress in Kimaragang seems to be neither contrastive nor fully predictable. Stress.. may fall on either the penultimate or the final syllable' (p. 4).
Stub; cites Ethnologue only; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul. 2013 (rev.). Dusun-Murut vowel harmony. Paper presented at ICAL 12; sec. 4.1, p. 17.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not about Klias River Kadazan. Same generalization: Bonggi and Tombonuwo 'have consistently penultimate stress'; Labuk Kadazan 'also has penultimate stress'; Kimaragang and Penampang Kadazan (Miller 1993) 'neither contrastive nor fully predictable. Stress is always either penultimate or final' (p. 17). Klias/Beaufort Kadazan not mentioned; Tatana' only in the bibliography.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Dusun/"Kadazan" Klias' (KLIAS) is one of Lobel's surveyed Southwest Sabah varieties and appears in pronoun/functor tables and the *R reflex tables (ch. 11, pp. 365 ff.), but there is no phonological sketch of it and no stress statement; the only stress/accent discussion (sec. 8.2.9 'Contrastive accent', p. 259) concerns Manide and Inagta Alabat in the Philippines.

sources.note: Nothing. Both chapters are lexicostatistics (PSC figures for Takuli BT, Tahak BT, Pinopok BT, Mandangin BT, Kinamam BT) and intelligibility testing; Banker & Banker (p. 308, pp. 332-334) split Klias River Kadazan off as a separate language on intelligibility grounds. A a full-text search for stress/accent the whole 1.7 MB volume text for stress/accent/penult (incl. scanned-spaced spellings) gives zero hits.
Lists only Smith 1984 (pp. 26-40), Banker & Banker 1984 and Ethnologue; no phonology or grammar reference exists for this language in Glottolog.
